tips: Load Suica to Apple/Google Wallet while still at MSP gate; land with transit ready.
Hit the konbini first, drop bags, then ramen — order via the English vending machine at Ichiran to avoid the line chaos.

2026-12-16.weatherAlert: December evenings in Shibuya are cold and windy; the Blue Cave walk along Yoyogi Park offers zero wind protection.

suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Miyashita Park covered rooftop + Parco + Tower Records
suggestedSwap.reason: If the cold wind is biting or it rains, the open-air Blue Cave walk is miserable; Miyashita Park's covered rooftop and indoor shops absorb a wet/freezing afternoon without surfacing.

tips: Shibuya Sky sunset slots sell out fast; if you can't book, Mag's Park rooftop is a cheap/free flex with great crossing views.
Pre-download the Purikura app filters so your 8-person booth session goes smoothly.

2026-12-17.weatherAlert: Risk of cold rain in the afternoon could dampen the Ueno Ameyoka outdoor market stroll.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Ueno Ameyoko market under the tracks
suggestedSwap.reason: If it rains, the open-air Ameyoko market is less enjoyable; the Tokyo National Museum is perfectly positioned between Asakusa and Akiba on the same line for a dry, world-class 2-hour break.

tips: Skytree night slots have insane queues; if the line is apocalyptic, pivot to Asahi Beer Hall's 22F Sky Room next door for the same river view with a beer in hand.
Kamiya Bar in Asakusa offers the famous Denki Bran 'electric brandy' for ~¥350 — a perfect pre-Skytree warm-up.
teamLab Planets requires stepping into water; wear easy-slip shoes and roll up your pants.
Golden Gai bars are tiny — split into groups of 2-4 to actually fit inside the 6-seat establishments.

2026-12-19.weatherAlert: High risk of cold, wet weather on the coast. The Enoshima island climb and Fuji-over-Sagami-Bay view are completely weather-dependent.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Enoshima island — climb to the Sea Candle
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Enoshima onsen finish: Enospa overlooks the bay
suggestedSwap.reason: If it's raining or bitterly cold, climbing an exposed island is brutal; Enospa offers a warm soak with the same bay views, saving your legs for the trip.

tips: If the Kamakura/Enoshima weather forecast looks grim on Dec 18, pivot to the Fuji Excursion train to Kawaguchiko — December offers peak clarity for that lake-reflection shot.
The Enoden coastal tram is charming but slow; if running late, skip the tram and take the JR Shonan-Shinjuku line directly back to Shinjuku.
Run the Airbnb washer during dinner so everyone lands in Kyoto with a clean kit.
Pack FIRST before hitting Golden Gai for the encore — bags must close tonight for the morning shinkansen sprint.

2026-12-21.weatherAlert: Rain is possible in the afternoon; Nishiki Market and Teramachi are mostly covered, but the Gion golden hour walk could be wet.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Gion at golden hour — Hanamikoji + Shirakawa canal
suggestedSwap.reason: If heavy rain hits in the afternoon, walking the exposed Gion streets is miserable; the Manga Museum (housed in an old school) is a massive, dry, indoor time vortex perfectly situated for the weather pivot.

tips: Sit on the LEFT side of the Nozomi shinkansen for the Mt. Fuji view around minute 40 out of Tokyo.
Nintendo Kyoto in Takashimaya is 5 min from Nishiki — scout today, buy in Osaka to avoid carrying merch on the train.

2026-12-22.weatherAlert: December mornings at Fushimi Inari are freezing; the exposed summit loop can be dangerously cold and slippery if frost is present.

suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Tōfuku-ji audible: Zen gardens + Tsutenkyo bridge
suggestedSwap.reason: If there is a cold snap or freezing rain, the steep, exposed trails of Fushimi Inari can be hazardous; Tōfuku-ji is just one stop away, offers stunning December Zen gardens, and is far less physically demanding in extreme cold.

tips: Vending machine hot corn soup on the descent is not a joke — it's a survival tactic.
Funaoka Onsen has an 'electric bath' — brace yourself, it's a uniquely shocking Japanese sento experience.

2026-12-23.weatherAlert: Rain makes the Arashiyama Bamboo Grove photos look flat and the Iwatayama Monkey Park climb dangerously slippery.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Iwatayama Monkey Park — humans enter the cage
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Kimono Forest at Randen Arashiyama station
suggestedSwap.reason: If it rains, the steep 20-min hike up to Monkey Park is a muddy slip hazard; the Kimono Forest at the nearby Randen station is free, covered, and offers beautiful glowing pillar-lit photos without the climb.

tips: Wakakusa-yama in Nara is CLOSED for the winter (closes 2nd Sunday of Dec) — do NOT attempt the climb.
Bow to the deer first, show empty hands when done; they understand the gesture and will respect the boundary.
Pre-order your KFC Christmas Bucket NOW if you haven't — December 24th buckets sell out weeks in advance for the sacred tradition.
If you missed the Nintendo Museum lottery, Uji's Byodo-in and Tsuen tea offer a beautiful, low-stress morning alternative.

2026-12-25.crowdAlert: USJ on Christmas Day will be at maximum capacity; Super Nintendo World timed entries will be gone within minutes of park opening.
tips: Rope-drop 45 minutes early and sprint to SNW; if Express Passes are sold out, rely on single-rider lines (saves ~60% on Mario Kart wait).
Kinopio's Cafe will have a massive queue; grab a Yoshi snack stand popcorn bucket and keep moving if the line is apocalyptic.

2026-12-26.weatherAlert: Miyajima island is highly exposed to cold, biting sea winds; the ferry ride and torii viewing can be brutal in December.
tips: This is the longest day of the trip — if anyone is redlining, skip Miyajima, do the Peace Museum unhurried, and meet at Hiroshima station.
The Peace Museum hits heavy; Shukkei-en garden is a quiet, beautiful 10-min walk from the station if the group needs a reflective breather.

2026-12-27.weatherAlert: The Midosuji Illumination is a 4km outdoor walk; if it rains, it becomes a miserable march.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: MIDOSUJI ILLUMINATION — 4km of lit boulevard, walked south
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Spa World audible: Shinsekai's gloriously kitsch mega-bath
suggestedSwap.reason: If it's pouring, walking 4km of illuminated boulevard is no fun; Spa World in Shinsekai offers a warm, indoor recovery move with Roman-themed baths and water slides to soak away 13 days of walking.

tips: Buy 551 Horai butaman (pork buns) from Namba station BEFORE the crab dinner — they sell out nightly and house breakfast depends on it.
Split squads for the afternoon: Den Den Town for the nerds, Amerikamura for the hypebeasts, regroup at Umeda Sky Building for sunset.
Do your tax-free paperwork check tonight: ensure receipts are with passports and purchases are accessible — customs CAN ask on exit.
If Kobe beef lunch breaks the budget, $22 Kobe-beef bowls and croquette stands around Sannomiya deliver 70% of the experience at 40% of the price.
Sit on the LEFT side of the Nozomi (Seats A) for Mt. Fuji's encore view out of Tokyo.
Zero-out your Suica cards and do final boss gachapon at the gate; Japanese whisky allocations at duty-free (Hibiki/Yamazaki) beat US prices badly if you find them.

globalTips: With the USD/JPY rate at ~161, your dollar stretches far—withdraw large lump sums at 7-Eleven ATMs to minimize per-transaction fees rather than making daily small withdrawals.

December in Japan is cold and dry, but coastal and outdoor sites (Enoshima, Miyajima, Arashiyama) face biting winds and occasional rain—pack a windproof outer layer and a compact travel umbrella, not just heavy coats.

For major transit days (Hiroshima, Himeji), check your JR Pass coverage; Nozomi trains are NOT covered by the standard JR Pass, so you'll need to pay the limited express fee or take the slightly slower Hikari trains.
